android.desc:
Manage your communication preferences with TRAI DND - the official Do Not Disturb (DND) preference management app developed by Telecom Regulatory Authority of India (TRAI).

The app enables mobile users to register, manage, and update their DND preferences, helping ensure that commercial communications are delivered in line with user consent, while allowing important and service-related messages to reach customers appropriately.

Key Features
-   ⁠Register for Full DND or Partial DND
-   Select categories of communication you wish to receive or restrict
-   Quick activation through OTP verification
-   View and update your current DND status
-   Simple, secure, and easy-to-use interface

Why Use TRAI DND?
-   Helps manage communication preferences effectively
-   Supports responsible and consent-based communication
-   Aligns with TRAI's telecom and commercial communication regulations
-   Ensures a consistent experience across mobile networks

Who Is This App For?
This app is useful for:
-   Mobile users who wish to manage their communication preferences
-   Ensuring smoother and more transparent communication delivery

Download TRAI DND to manage your communication preferences and support a more trusted and compliant telecom ecosystem.

quotes.text:
If you are Indian, its so much easier to report spam (but of course not easy enough! TRAI, while seems to have good intentions here, is pretty much a luddite where tech & UX are concerned).

make sure your number is register in DnD.
Use the official DnD app to register a compliant https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=trai.gov.in.dnd&hl=en_IN&gl=US

The app rating should have given you a clue that the app is quite a crapfest, but it is still better than the steps folks in US have to wade through. it takes a couple of clicks and a short few typed words to raise the complaint.

Another way is to simply send a sms to 1909 as

> “<Content of UCC, including Referred Telephone Number (RTN) if any>,
<header/telephone number from which UCC has originated>, <dd/mm/yy, hh:mm>”

the schema is different for all ISPs, but in general none seems to adhere strictly to the schema as long as the datetime, phone number and comma delimiters are correct.

Here is the link from airtel on the way to file such complaints; https://www.airtel.in/business/commercial-communication/assets/documents/Help_Modules/Cop_docs/CoP_Complaints_08_11_2018.pdf

ISPs are required by law to folloup on these and once you have sent the sms, you will get update smses for your complaint.

I usually just use the DnD app and when that isn't working, I send the sms. the schema i can get from my sms history and just change the caller id, phone and date. And in return I get the satisfaction of getting the update …

quotes.text:
Looks like TRAI (Telecom Regulatory Authority of India) has an Android version of the app as well (https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=trai.gov.in.dnd). Permissions requested by the Android app seem to be very broad (Reading call log, Sending & Receiving SMS etc.) If they tried the same thing with Apple, I am not surprised that Apple has blocked their app. Such permissions can be used to easily snoop on a user's activity by Government entities.

What Mr.Sharma does not seem to get is Apple is very particular about user privacy. In the past users have been tricked into giving out their private data or scammed into subscribing to really expensive subscriptions by scammy apps (http://thehackernews.com/2017/06/apple-subscription-scam.html)

I am not saying TRAI's app is going to scam users but Apple's concern is genuine. TRAI can work around it by changing the away the app collects the spam call data from a user's phone. They certainly don't need the entire call history.

Here's where things get odd. TRAI has a tough job on its hands too. They cannot simply allow users to report any phone numbers as spam callers without verifying it. The reason is simple. It opens up the possibility of misuse via fraudulent reports. Those who have dealt with the Indian market will recall that fraud is rampant in the system - both by users as well as businesses.
quotes.story_title: Apple’s Refusal to Approve India’s Anti-Spam App Angers Regulators
